why: The statement is a universal, unrestricted claim that the supremum of local Lyapunov dimension over a global attractor is attained at an equilibrium or periodic orbit. A single explicit system whose maximum sits only on an invariant torus (4+4/c against at most 3) contradicts it, so Colbrook's preprint answers the whole question in the negative: scope whole, direction refuted, object a counterexample. It is unreviewed: the only human check is the author's own, and the Lean build is not digestion (F7). The dimension values also need the paper's argument, so it is not 'checkable'. It is credible: the author is an established researcher, the formalisation is substantial and no specific error has been identified; 19 days of silence is not a reason for doubt. The AI role is generated, because the author's declaration says Codex was used 'to obtain the counterexample'. ChatGPT 6's quoted role (discussions, Lean assistance) is thin and earns nothing on its own. The Lean repository formalises the same argument and adds no mathematics, so its scope is none and, being formalisation work, its AI role is none. Kressner–Vandereycken is a different conjecture (variant). The pre-2024 single-system verifications are instances, and the Hénon self-excited results address Kuznetsov's refinement (variant).
doubts: The close call is the competing reading: whether Eden's conjecture means the unrestricted statement or the literature's restricted or self-excited forms. I answered on the bullet's wording, which is unrestricted; the paper's own title concedes that a restricted form remains open. The AI quote and the theorem statement reach the record through repository files and a summarising fetch, not the PDF itself, so they are not verbatim-checked. The Palomar registry entry is unconfirmed. Verification for the pre-snapshot journal papers is assumed from journal publication as cited by Wikipedia; it does not affect the outcome.
